question.text: A wire of density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> is stretched between two clamps <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> apart. The resulting strain in the wire is  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><mo>×</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The lowest frequency of the transverse vibrations in the wire (Young's modulus of wire  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>9</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>10</mn></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi>Nm</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> ), (to the nearest integer),_______
